_about: The inventory of what Milky's editor understands, and how each construct is drawn.
Rendered on /design and mirrored in DesignSystem/README.md. Keep it honest:
if the tokenizer doesn't handle something, it belongs under `unsupported`, not `blocks`.
principles: The source is the document. There is no preview mode, and so no second representation to keep in sync.
Punctuation is dimmed, never deleted. The asterisks around bold text stay in the file and stay on screen — they just step back until the caret enters that line.
Nothing rewrites your file. Bullets and checkboxes are drawn on top of the literal hyphen and bracket characters; the bytes on disk are exactly what you typed.
Where a construct cannot be laid out in a plain-text editor — a table's column alignment — the source is set monospaced so hand-alignment works, rather than faked.

blocks.name: Heading
blocks.render: Scaled and bolded; the # dims to a margin mark

blocks.name: Paragraph
blocks.render: Body face; blank lines set the block rhythm

blocks.name: Blockquote
blocks.render: Indented, italic, with a drawn rule in the margin
blocks.note: Nested `> >` parses but is not drawn deeper

blocks.name: Bulleted list
blocks.render: A drawn bullet over the hidden marker; hanging indent

blocks.name: Ordered list
blocks.render: Number in the accent ink; Return continues and increments

blocks.name: Task list
blocks.render: A drawn circle or filled accent disc with a tick

blocks.name: Table
blocks.render: Monospaced rows, bold header, dimmed pipes and rule row
blocks.note: Alignment markers parse but cannot move text in a plain-text editor

blocks.name: Horizontal rule
blocks.render: A drawn hairline; the characters themselves go clear

blocks.name: Frontmatter
blocks.syntax: --- at the top of a file
blocks.render: Monospaced and dimmed, treated as metadata not prose

blocks.name: Footnote
blocks.render: Reference raised and small; definition in the accent ink

blocks.name: Hard break
blocks.render: Underlined, because the source is otherwise invisible

blocks.name: Display math
blocks.syntax: $$ on its own line, then TeX
blocks.render: Typeset in New York across the lines between the fences
blocks.note: A TeX subset — see Math below

inline.name: Bold
inline.render: Weight merged onto whatever the block already set

inline.name: Italic
inline.render: Italic; intraword underscores are left alone

inline.name: Link
inline.render: Label in the system blue; the URL dims away

inline.render: Accent ink — internal navigation, not a URL

inline.render: A pill; collected into the sidebar

unsupported.name: Setext headings
unsupported.why: The underline form collides with horizontal rules and frontmatter, and almost nobody types it.

unsupported.name: Reference links
unsupported.why: Rarely written by hand; the inline form covers the same ground.

unsupported.name: Inline and block HTML
unsupported.why: Notes are prose. Rendering HTML would mean a second representation to keep in sync.

unsupported.name: Emoji shortcodes
unsupported.why: macOS has a system emoji picker; the literal character round-trips everywhere.

math._about: Why this is not KaTeX, and what the subset covers.
approach: KaTeX is JavaScript. Running it would mean a WKWebView per formula inside an NSTextView — slow, and hostile to inline math.
Instead a small TeX-subset typesetter produces attributes and glyph substitutions, so an equation lives in the same text storage as the prose around it.

Nothing is rewritten. `\alpha` is six characters that draw as one α and five nothings, using the layout manager's glyph substitution. Select it, copy it, save it — you get back exactly what you typed.
The caret's own line shows its source, the same reveal every other construct uses. There is always a way to see and edit the TeX.
supported: Around 150 commands: Greek, operators, relations, set theory, logic, big operators, arrows.
Superscripts and subscripts, including nested ones and commands as bodies (x^\infty).
TeX conventions: single letters italic, digits and function names upright.
limits: Fractions do not stack. \frac{a}{b} draws as a⁄b, because a true two-level fraction needs its own line layout.
Matrices, alignment environments and \begin{…} are not handled.
A symbol no available font can draw leaves its whole expression as source rather than showing a half-substituted line.
Currency is protected: a dollar followed by a space, or preceded by one at the close, is prose — so "$5 and $10" stays text.

syntaxRoles.what: Declarations and control flow. Carries the brand hue.
